useBoundary: Generated exact-record projection, not independently updated authority. Use all three explicit case sources together. Source metadata and URLs are dated references, not proof this job fetched current official law. Cite the fetched projection as Notary Geek analysis; recheck controlling sources before acting. A job covers only its named claim IDs, never the entire audit or every transaction.

interpretationRules.purpose: Each evidence limit applies to a particular question. Preserve both the established finding and its limit; do not use an unrelated uncertainty, hypothetical defense or credential to erase a documented contradiction. Revise a finding when relevant evidence answers it, and identify exactly what changed.

rules.risk: Treating an unobserved signing session as a reason to dismiss a documented public legal error.
rules.requiredReading: No session inspection limits conclusions about a particular notary’s act. It does not undo the six source-backed contradictions identified in this review. Evaluate the published rule against the cited authority and date; evaluate a particular act against its separate record.
rules.doesNotEstablish: The audit does not prove a particular act defective, and lack of that proof does not establish that the published assurance is correct.

rules.risk: Turning a performed check into proof of law.
rules.requiredReading: A provider may use KBA, fingerprints, a selfie or additional checks. Identify whether the governing law required that check, whether it qualifies as the claimed statutory method, and whether the complete process satisfied that method. Technical operation and legal sufficiency are different propositions. An optional authorized method need not be universally mandatory.
rules.doesNotEstablish: A successful check, vendor name or assurance label alone proves neither statutory authorization nor compliance; voluntary additional checks are not thereby prohibited.

rules.risk: Treating a possible earlier route as an established historical defense.
rules.requiredReading: KBA was expressly added effective July 1, 2024. A provider asserting another earlier route must identify its then-applicable authority, adoption history and complete method evidence. The unresolved IMSAC chain is a research lead; mentioning KBA/biometrics in guidance does not establish that authority or the provider’s compliance.
rules.doesNotEstablish: Do not replace the proven express-addition date with an assumption of unchanged law. This record also does not prove that every earlier KBA-assisted act violated the law.

rules.risk: Using retroactive validation to claim that original duties were met or the criticism no longer matters.
rules.requiredReading: The validation rule concerns legal effect and preserves stated challenges/remedies. It does not establish what method ran, what the historical law required, whether a duty was met or whether a marketed legal rule was accurate.
rules.doesNotEstablish: Neither automatic invalidity nor automatic compliance follows. A commissioned notary’s method failure is not automatically an unauthorized-person case.

rules.risk: Using MISMO review, IAL2, SOC 2 or a title-market requirement as legal approval.
rules.requiredReading: Recognize the credential’s actual scope. MISMO performs standards review and excludes jurisdiction-specific legal verification; a named IAL2 level still needs version/configuration/assessment and statutory mapping. A procurement contract can require a credential without making it proof of the notarial method.
rules.doesNotEstablish: A private assessment not obtained by this review is neither disproved nor presumed favorable evidence for the missing legal proposition. Standards compliance, company reputation and transaction compliance are not interchangeable.

rules.risk: Letting a qualification elsewhere cure a contradictory categorical summary.
rules.requiredReading: Preserve accurate conditions where the article states them. The body’s alternative-method discussion does not make a table’s universal CA/KBA rule accurate. Application/technology-description review does not become Secretary platform-compliance approval.
rules.doesNotEstablish: This review does not call every sentence false or deny every administrative review. Neither concession answers the particular false assurance.

rules.risk: Treating corrections to our draft or a count of supported entries as exoneration of the remaining findings.
rules.requiredReading: The review corrected onboarding, workflow-policy and qualified document examples and acknowledged NotaryCam’s IAL2 statement. Those repairs apply to those entries. Assess each remaining false finding on its own evidence; supported propositions do not cancel unrelated contradictions.
rules.doesNotEstablish: Seventy-seven entries are not seventy-seven errors, and there is no valid vote-count rule under which correct statements erase material false ones.

rules.risk: Using incomplete page capture to call independently identified contradictions unsupported.
rules.requiredReading: The missing original-page snapshot limits exhaustive version-specific coverage and publication-history claims. It does not erase the identified representations, including text supplied by the user and checked against retrieved first-party text, or their comparison with official authorities. A contrary dated capture should be examined proposition by proposition.
rules.doesNotEstablish: No complete forensic capture is claimed. A later correction does not by itself show that the earlier representation was accurate, and an audit hash does not authenticate the original page.

rules.risk: Using intent, company size or widespread practice to avoid answering a false assurance.
rules.requiredReading: The source-quality objection concerns the accuracy of the assurance sold. It does not require a finding of criminal intent. Evaluate the representation and applicable law; familiarity, market share, early entry, commercial acceptance or the critic’s small size do not answer that question. Unknown intent does not establish either knowing deception or good faith.
rules.doesNotEstablish: The audit does not establish every actor’s motive or every competitor’s historical effort. That limit is not a defense of the identified false statement, and calling the pattern theater does not answer it.

rules.risk: Treating official handbook shorthand as permission to ignore enacted requirements.
rules.requiredReading: The current handbook is relevant guidance and reliance context. When a summary conflicts with the controlling statute, identify and resolve the conflict rather than treating the summary’s official origin as proof that a statutory condition disappears.
rules.doesNotEstablish: The handbook does not itself establish a provider’s actual method or cure its public assertion. This finding does not deny the evidentiary value of agency guidance.

rules.risk: Dismissing the issue as a Virginia technicality or assuming a different state solves it.
rules.requiredReading: Virginia is this provider-selected case study. A method condition can determine whether a marketed assurance is true. The same dated authority-and-method inquiry applies in Texas and other states; correct performance would remove the need to sell Virginia as a compliance shortcut.
rules.doesNotEstablish: The record does not establish a fifty-state violation, Texas compliance, or another provider’s fitness. A broader research gap does not diminish this page’s established errors.

rules.risk: Reducing a false compliance assurance to harmless wording because no injury or deliberate deception was proved.
rules.requiredReading: The page presents legal rules and review/certification signals to guide platform selection. A source-backed contradiction in that guidance remains a substantive accuracy problem requiring correction. A possible editorial mistake, obsolete source or automated drafting process is an explanation to investigate, not proof the assurance was true.
rules.doesNotEstablish: This audit does not establish an injured customer, actual buyer reliance, liability or how the article was authored. Those separate questions do not need to be resolved before identifying and correcting the false representation.

rules.risk: Using possible logo permission, public-domain government works or possible conformity to dismiss the official-assurance concern.
rules.requiredReading: Evaluate the observed trust presentation separately from authorization and technical conformity. General government-work reuse does not authorize agency-logo use. Possible permission is not obtained permission; actual permission does not create endorsement. NIST’s lack of a Digital Identity Guidelines certification program does not disprove an independent assessment. Neither the logo nor an assessment supplies the statutory identity method.
rules.doesNotEstablish: The audit does not establish unauthorized logo use, a government enforcement decision or failed IAL2 conformity. Those limits do not turn the agency logo into proof of certification, approval or legal compliance.

rules.risk: Treating framework-derived practices, a confidential report or absence of a known breach as proof of the advertised security outcome.
rules.requiredReading: Separate claimed practice, implemented control, scoped assessment and advertised outcome. Report confidentiality does not prove absence; it also does not permit inventing a favorable opinion or unlimited coverage. NIST is unspecified here, so do not silently select CSF 2.0 or IAL2 as the full security baseline. Recognize SOC 2’s assurance scope without reducing the objection to terminology. The overstatement can be corrected without first demonstrating a security incident.
rules.doesNotEstablish: The audit does not establish a breach, ineffective encryption, nonexistent audits or failed conformity. Even established security-control effectiveness would not itself prove the statutory identity method or notarial-law compliance.

rules.risk: Weakening a NIST SHALL NOT to a preference, or using statutory KBA, terminology, an older revision or hypothetical extra checks as automatic conformity clearance.
rules.requiredReading: Read the current identity-verification restriction together with the distinct fraud-management permission and documented tailoring process. The rule names both KBV and KBA; renaming the quiz does not avoid it. Historical analysis must include Revision 3’s FAQ excluding KBV as satisfying IAL2/IAL3 verification. Identify the actual qualifying verification method and any compensating-control evidence rather than inventing them. Preserve the distinction between state-law notarial duties and voluntarily claimed technical conformity.
rules.doesNotEstablish: The baseline prohibition does not ban every use of knowledge questions or determine state-law validity. Permitted fraud checks and documented deviations do not by themselves prove the provider follows them, satisfy unmodified baseline verification, or authorize the NIST agency logo.

limitations: No completed signing, identity document, biometric template, private customer record or confidential audit report was inspected. A page error does not establish which method a particular notary used or the legal effect of a particular act. Conversely, the absence of those records does not establish compliant performance or turn a source-backed false legal representation into an unresolved transaction question.
No complete fifty-state identity-law survey was performed. The article’s broad interstate generalization is unsupported as presented, rather than replaced with the opposite generalization.

Private certification can have contractual or procurement significance. This audit does not claim it has no possible legal relevance; it establishes that the certification itself is not a state-law compliance determination.
Some provider, MISMO and USCIS pages were available through indexed official/first-party text while direct fetches returned 403. Access limitations are recorded per source; indexed content may lag.

The page’s authorship process and the motives or historical efforts of every competing provider were not established. The findings about false and unsupported claims stand on their sources independently of intent.
The article was reviewed on October 2, 2026. Later edits, actual product availability and any subsequent legislative changes require a new dated review.

This work is public source analysis, not a legal opinion on a customer’s transaction. It does not claim all prior acts are invalid. The limited validation rule and retained remedies in § 47.1-20.1 must be analyzed separately.

Entry totals count analytical findings, including supported propositions, overlaps and supplemental context; they are not counts of unique false article statements. VA24 and PC07 address the same KBA-timing representation from different analytical angles.

The original page version was not preserved. Article locations are textual section/row descriptions, not immutable paragraph identifiers. Reacquire a dated full-page capture before claiming exhaustive version-specific coverage; no hash of this audit authenticates the original webpage.

Express KBA enumeration in 2024 does not by itself determine whether an earlier implemented process qualified under another then-authorized method. Official identity guidance is a possible authority-chain lead; applicable adoption history and actual method compliance remain to be established. A factor’s use or mention in guidance does not prove it was required or legally sufficient.

investigationFrame.primaryIssue: Platform and industry assurances substituted for the applicable law and actual transaction evidence.
investigationFrame.whyVirginiaHere: The provider selected Virginia’s history and purported flexibility as a commercial assurance. This case study tests that assurance.
broaderScope: Other commissioned states and advertised identity workflows
investigationFrame.texasFindingStatus: A broader research lead; this Virginia-page audit does not purport to resolve Texas law or particular Texas sessions.
investigationFrame.desiredOutcome: Correct methods and technology under the governing law would remove the need to sell Virginia as a special compliance shortcut.
